question.problem: Let $T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 7 & 0 \\ -3 & 9 & 0 \\ 4 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}]$ be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 15 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
The vector $v$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T)$ if there exists a vector $u=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]$  such that $T(u)=v.$

Therefore, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot u & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & 7 & 0 \\ -3 & 9 & 0 \\ 4 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 15 \\ k\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2x+7y \\ -3x+9y \\ 4x-5y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 15 \\ k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2x+7y=12 \\ -3x+9y=15 \\ 4x-5y=k.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $x=3y-5$, which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+7y & =12 \\ -2(3y-5)+7y & =12 \\ y & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3y-5 \\  & =3(2)-5 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=1$ and $y=2$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-5y & =k \\ 4(1)-5(2) & =k \\ k & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $v\in \text{Im}(T)$ when $k=-6.$
